q: AGENTS.md:94 says a goose feature is validated by:
options: Updating goose-self-test.yaml, rebuilding, then running `goose run --recipe goose-self-test.yaml`
Running cargo test with the nightly toolchain
Opening a draft PR and waiting for the bot
Running the win32 installer build
explanation: Nightly rustc is never part of the validation rule.
Bot review is not the validation step the rule names.
Installer builds are release engineering, not feature validation.

q: Why does the rule order "rebuild" BEFORE running the recipe?
options: The recipe run launches the freshly built binary, so the new behavior must be compiled in first
cargo refuses to download crates otherwise
The recipe file embeds the target/ directory hash
Rebuilding resets the RUST_LOG caches
explanation: Downloads have nothing to do with recipe execution.
Recipe files carry no build-hash coupling.
RUST_LOG is env-filter based, unrelated to compile state.

q: goose-self-test.yaml's top-level skeleton includes which block for run-time inputs?
options: parameters (keys like test_phases and test_depth with defaults and descriptions)
secrets
dependencies
harness binary path
explanation: The file has no secrets block.
Recipes are prompts, not dependency manifests.
No harness path exists; the recipe runs through goose itself.

q: What problem does the feature template force you to answer FIRST?
options: What problem would this solve — the outcome before any implementation talk
Which branch the PR will target
How many lines the diff will contain
What the commit message will be
explanation: Branch targeting is decided after the idea is accepted.
Line counts are irrelevant at proposal stage.
Commit message craft comes at ship time, not proposal time.

q: A minimal `fit_label` must truncate by `chars().take(max_chars)` rather than byte-slicing because:
options: Byte-slicing can split a multibyte character: either a panic or invalid UTF-8 labeled output
Byte slicing is slower by a constant factor
chars().take() allocates less memory than slicing always
Clippy denies all slicing regardless of the index type
explanation: The difference is correctness on Unicode, not speed.
take().collect() can allocate too; the win is boundary safety.
clippy warns on string_slice; it does not deny all slicing semantics.

q: A recipe like workflow_recipes/release_risk_check/recipe.yaml is best described as:
options: An executable maintainer ritual: a YAML with parameters and instructions that goose runs as a task
A CI workflow definition identical to .github/workflows files
A dependency lockfile variant
A markdown-style checklist for humans only
explanation: Workflow recipes are distinct from GitHub Actions definitions.
Lockfiles pin dependencies; recipes encode tasks.
They exist to be run BY goose, not just read by humans.

q: Fix this mini-cycle failure: your feature's tests pass, but the feature was never added to goose-self-test.yaml. The risk a maintainer will flag:
options: Unit-pass but session-fail — no live-goose scenario proves the feature is discoverable and usable end-to-end
The binary will not link without a recipe entry
cargo test silently skips crates not listed in recipes
The PR becomes unmergeable until a recipe reviewer title matches
explanation: Linking is a build concern, unrelated to recipe entries.
cargo test does not consult recipe files at all.
No bot blocks on title matching; the gap is verification coverage.
